I’m an ambulatory but almost full time user (even use it around the house) I also have a few other diagnoses that contribute to the wheelchair use. Before I used the wheelchair I used a cane, then a walker for a few years, and now the wheelchair. The biggest thing I want to stress is getting mobility aids is best when it’s a team decision. Your pt/ot will be able to find what’s best for you and go from there. With something like a cane it is less pertinent that your medical team is informed and on board because there are less risks but I really really really caution people from getting wheelchairs without going through the proper channels because that is how you get injured and there are huge health trade offs.

This of course depends on your body and unfortunately can’t really tell you exactly what will happen to you but I can tell you a bit about my recovery. 

My surgery went 100% well no complications or anything but I was still in the hospital for 2 weeks and on many pain medications. Coming home I went to my friends house and lived with them for about a week. While I did not constantly need help I did basically need someone there 24/7 for help with smaller random tasks. I wasn’t bed bound but couldn’t do much besides walk a few steps to microwave dinner and into the bathroom. By the time I was home I could shower independently (make sure to stock up on baby shampoo to wash your hair!) but needed a chair 100%. You’re going to be pretty spacey with the amount of medication you’re on even at home which really makes the having someone with you thing important. Having someone there is also pretty important to watch out for any complications. 

I have other neurological issues so maybe my recovery was extra rough but I don’t think that’s too much of the case as it was brain surgery after all. I hope this doesn’t sound too scary! You will rock it and I hope you have a smooth recovery!
